arxiv-2209-00153.title: Global regularity and decay behavior for Leray equations with critical-dissipation and Its Application to Self-similar Solutions
arxiv-2209-00153.creator: Changxing Miao, Xiaoxin Zheng
arxiv-2209-00153.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Changxing Miao, Xiaoxin Zheng. In this paper, we show the global regularity and the optimal decay of weak solutions to the generalized Leray problem with critical dissipation. Our method is based on the maximal smoothing effect, L p L^{p} -type elliptic regularity of linearization, and the action of the heat semigroup generated by the fractional powers of Laplace operator on distributions with Fourier transforms supported in an annulus.

arxiv-2404-09908.title: Spatially disordered environments stabilize competitive metacommunities
arxiv-2404-09908.creator: Prajwal Padmanabha, Giorgio Nicoletti, Davide Bernardi, Samir Suweis, Sandro Azaele, Andrea Rinaldo, Amos Maritan
arxiv-2404-09908.description: Abstract Metapopulation models have been instrumental in demonstrating the ecological impact of landscape structure on the survival of a focal species in complex environments. However, extensions to multiple species with arbitrary dispersal networks often rely on phenomenological assumptions limiting their scope.

arxiv-2404-10582.title: Roles of band gap and Kane electronic dispersion in the THz-frequency nonlinear optical response in HgCdTe
arxiv-2404-10582.creator: Davide Soranzio, Elsa Abreu, Sarah Houver, Janine Dössegger, Matteo Savoini, Frédéric Teppe, Sergey Krishtopenko, Nikolay N. Mikhailov, Sergey A. Dvoretsky, Steven L. Johnson
arxiv-2404-10582.description: Abstract Materials with linear electronic dispersion often feature high carrier mobilities and unusually strong nonlinear optical interactions. In this work, we investigate the THz nonlinear dynamics of one such material, HgCdTe, with an electronic band dispersion heavily dependent on both temperature and stoichiometry.

arxiv-2409-07925.title: A framework for measuring the training efficiency of a neural architecture
arxiv-2409-07925.creator: Eduardo Cueto-Mendoza, John Kelleher
arxiv-2409-07925.description: Abstract Measuring Efficiency in neural network system development is an open research problem. This paper presents an experimental framework to measure the training efficiency of a neural architecture. To demonstrate our approach, we analyze the training efficiency of Convolutional Neural Networks and Bayesian equivalents on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 tasks.

pmc-11483811.title: Uranium Repartitioning during Microbial Driven Reductive Transformation of U(VI)-Sorbed Schwertmannite and Jarosite
pmc-11483811.creator: Changxun Yu, Anders Johnson, Andreas Karlsson, Roman Chernikov, Viktor Sjöberg, Zhaoliang Song, Mark Dopson, Mats E. Åström
pmc-11483811.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study exposes U(VI)-sorbed schwertmannite and jarosite to biotic reductive incubations under field-relevant conditions and examines the changes in aqueous and solid-phase speciation of U, Fe, and S as well as associated microbial communities over 180 days.

pmc-12748092.title: Paradigm shift in patients with multiple brain metastases from whole brain radiotherapy to high precision multimodality treatment including stereotactic radiotherapy
pmc-12748092.creator: Jeroen Crouzen, Mirjam Mast, Melissa Kerkhof, Maaike Vos, Thijs van der Vaart, Rishi Nandoe Tewarie, Rob Nabuurs, Ruud Wiggenraad, Mandy Kiderlen, Noëlle van der Voort van Zyp, Anna Petoukhova, Marike Broekman, Jaap Zindler
pmc-12748092.description: BackgroundWhole brain radiotherapy (WBRT) is increasingly being replaced by high precision multimodality treatment including stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) in patients with ≥ 4 brain metastases (BMs). The implications of this trend on survival rates are uncertain. Our study examines the time trends for survival rates of patients treated with radiotherapy for brain metastases during this era of shifting treatment paradigms.

pmc-12773326.title: Abstract 019: Effective Diagnostic Testing For Uncommon Etiologies Of Venous Pulsatile Tinnitus
pmc-12773326.creator: Sivani Lingam, Aaron Brake, Vince Galate, Robert Turner, Michael G Abraham
pmc-12773326.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionPulsatile Tinnitus (PT) is a rhythmic sound in the ears. It can be incapacitating and is even associated with depression and suicidal ideationi. The etiology of PT can be grouped into vascular and non‐vascular causes. ii,iii While prominent venous structures may be believed to be the underlying cause of PT, interventions on these structures do not always result in symptom resolution. Successful treatment is contingent on correctly identifying culpable vascular targets.

pmc-13048373.title: Signet-Ring Cell Carcinoma Masquerading as Crohn’s Disease: A Diagnostic Challenge in Multifocal Colonic Strictures with Ascites
pmc-13048373.creator: Ishan Antony, Markos Kalligeros, Samantha Zullow
pmc-13048373.description: Gastrointestinal malignancies such as signet-ring cell carcinoma can mimic inflammatory bowel disease, leading to diagnostic uncertainty. We present the case of a 39-year-old woman who presented with cramping abdominal pain, watery diarrhea, and unintentional weight loss. Imaging revealed multifocal colonic strictures and pelvic ascites, initially suspected to represent Crohn’s disease.

pmc-13131998.title: Foreign Body Granulomatous Reaction of the Breast Mimicking Carcinoma: A Radiologic-Pathologic Diagnostic Pitfall
pmc-13131998.creator: Yanina Nikolaus
pmc-13131998.description: Foreign body granulomatous reactions of the breast are uncommon benign entities that may closely mimic carcinoma on imaging. We report the case of a woman in her seventies who presented with persistent breast pain and an enlarging lesion detected on imaging.

pmc-13140947.title: Take a deep breath: managing the challenges of acute respiratory distress syndrome cases
pmc-13140947.creator: Manuel Castillo-Angeles, Ali Salim
pmc-13140947.description: SummaryAcute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains a major challenge in trauma care, with high morbidity and mortality. Current management emphasizes lung-protective ventilation, careful fluid balance, and a multidisciplinary approach. New areas of discovery, such as ARDS phenotyping, precision medicine, ECMO innovations, and evolving adjunctive therapies, are reshaping practice and offering opportunities for improved outcomes.

pmc-13291935.title: Revival of Mucin-Degrading Human-Derived Fecal Microbial Consortia After Cryopreservation
pmc-13291935.creator: Ava N. Tafreshi, Teanna Samuel, Gilberto E. Flores, Ashwana D. Fricker
pmc-13291935.description: Human gut microbial communities capable of degrading mucin are taxonomically unique and have a range of physiologically relevant metabolic outputs. To determine the feasibility of reviving mucin-degrading fecal microbial communities after cryopreservation, we employed 16S rRNA gene sequencing to characterize revived communities. Microbial communities were generally stable but small donor-dependent shifts in diversity, composition, and taxonomy were observed following revival.

pmc-13578085.title: Experiences and coping strategies of time toxicity in young and middle-aged patients with lymphoma: a descriptive qualitative study
pmc-13578085.creator: Danyang Li, Kexin Zheng, Lizhen Chen, Meiyun Zhang
pmc-13578085.description: BackgroundWith advancements in lymphoma treatment leading to improved survival rates, the time burden associated with cancer care has emerged as a significant concern. Time toxicity can disrupt daily life and impact treatment decisions; however, lymphoma-specific evidence regarding patients’ subjective experiences remains limited.
